purpose: Response-free paired known-truth test of whether evidence-driven pruning of incompatible worlds improves the same source-symmetric sequential contextual representation relative to retaining all declared worlds.

design.source_policy: two response-independent anchor nodes (minimum-x and maximum-x) persist; previous-context positives are added as sources before the next forecast
design.world_support: binary Euclidean reachability from the declared source set within threshold
design.response_truth: outside true-world support probability is exactly 0; inside true-world support probability is sigmoid(-0.35 + 0.45*node_covariate + 0.30*sin(context_phase) - 0.15*cos(context_phase))
design.layer_a_update_order: context t features use worlds surviving through t-1; after observing t positives, eliminate any world that failed to support at least one positive; eliminated worlds never return
design.conditioned_contextual_arm: source-symmetric contextual summary using only evidence-compatible surviving worlds
design.uncontracted_contextual_arm: same source-symmetric contextual summary using the full declared world set at every context, ignoring Layer-A elimination for prediction only
design.fit_policy: fit each arm once on all calibration node-context rows; do not refit during heldout contexts
design.primary_metric: macro binary log loss across the eight heldout contexts
design.secondary_metric: macro Brier score across heldout contexts

estimands.mechanism: whether response-history pruning of incompatible worlds improves the prediction-facing representation when source refresh, label invariance, outcomes, learner and baseline are held fixed

decision.next_if_supported: freeze a fresh response-blind real-system test selected before biological response access and persist the full Layer-A trajectory
decision.next_if_not_supported: do not add a no-contraction predictive gate; move to a different response-independent explanation axis

forbidden_interpretations: Synthetic effect magnitudes estimate Azores, Louisiana, Tampa or Portal effect sizes
Passing this benchmark proves contraction is necessary or sufficient in real ecological prediction
Passing authorizes reanalysis or rescue of Portal
Passing retroactively establishes that Azores contracted
This benchmark changes the closed EOG-WF empirical synthesis
